summary: Confirmed both specified semantic-similarity estimates against the paper. Read the complete markdown conversion, including Appendices A-E and references. Directly checked all cited PDF pages: p. 8, Sections 4.6 and 4.6.2; p. 9, Section 5.5; p. 10, Section 5.5.2; and p. 11, Table 7, also recovered with find_tables. All recorded statistics match the correct study and arms, including their printed precision, Study 1 p = 0.00, and the Study 2 negative-zero confidence limit. Participant counts are supported by the findings sections: Study 1 has 45 per arm and 90 total; Study 2 has 59 assisted, 58 human-only, and 117 total. Table 7 corroborates the included idea counts; Study 1 explicitly retains each participant's first idea, and Study 2 describes parallel analyses without reporting a different participant sample. Both records correctly code question=across_people, construct=diversity, measure=embedding_similarity, unit=pair, higher_is=more_similar, outcome_with_ai=true, outcome_timing=immediate, within_person=null, and comparison_type=ai_vs_bau. The permutation/resampling unit and treatment of dependence among pairs are unspecified throughout the paper, so se_basis=unclear is correct under the current rules. Unprinted pair counts, standard errors, SD level, and effect-size standardizers appropriately remain null. The Study 2 subtraction direction is appropriately left unresolved. The completeness check found no missing eligible outcome or contrast under rules 4-6: breadth, depth, semantic similarity, novelty, usefulness, creativity, and idea count are represented for both studies. The model-only comparisons and the unassignable qualitative statement about shorter ideas are documented in not_extracted.
